chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadhdha', who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far عليه السلام about a man who struck another man on his head with the pole of a tent in a single blow, causing a penetrating wound until the blow reached his brain, and his intellect departed. He said: "If the one struck does not comprehend the salat (prayer) because of it, and does not understand what he said nor what was said to him, then he is to be observed for a year. If he dies between that time and the year, his striker is subject to retaliation (qisas) for him. But if he does not die between that time and the year, and his intellect does not return to him, his striker must pay the blood money (diyyah) from his own wealth for the loss of his intellect."

He said: So I said to him: Then what do you hold against him regarding the head wound? He said: "No, because he only struck him a single blow, and that blow caused two injuries. So I imposed upon him the more severe of the two injuries, which is the blood money (diyyah). And if he had struck him with two blows, and the two blows caused two injuries, I would have imposed upon him the liability of what the two blows caused, whatever they may have been, except if death were in one of them, in which case his striker would be subject to retaliation (qisas) for it, and the other would be set aside."

He said: "And if he struck him three blows, one after another, and they caused three injuries, I would impose upon him the liability of what the three blows caused, whatever they may have been, so long as there was no death in them; then his striker would be subject to retaliation (qisas) for it."

He said: "And if he struck him ten blows and they caused a single injury, I would impose upon him that injury which the ten blows caused, whatever it may have been, so long as there was no death in it."

key_terms.أُقِيدَ بِهِ: retaliation (qisas) is carried out against the offender
key_terms.جِنَايَتَيْنِ: two injuries or offenses resulting from a harmful act
key_terms.ذَهَابِ عَقْلِهِ: loss of the victim's intellect or mental faculty
key_terms.سَنَةً: a one-year waiting period to observe the outcome of the injury
key_terms.ضَرْبَةً وَاحِدَةً: a single blow, legally treated as one act of striking
key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةَ: blood money; prescribed financial compensation for injury
key_terms.ٱلشَّجَّةِ: a head wound or wound to the skull/head

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person is struck on the head and loses his intellect in Shi'i fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling on bodily injury that results in loss of intellect, distinguishing between cases that lead to death and cases that do not. It also explains how liability is calculated when one blow causes multiple harms or when multiple blows cause one or more distinct injuries.
